    Maintenance audit — 2026-10-30

    Source: MAINTENANCE.md

    Hosted follow-up — 3 November 2026

    Baseline 3faf2712a031, hosted R check 41604839545: the macOS TIFF tests failed because CRAN R reported Cairo support but could not load its XQuartz runtime libraries. Enable the existing shared workflow’s macos-xquartz input and correct the platform prerequisites in the README. The workflow and its supported matrix are otherwise unchanged. The existing informational oldrel-3 dependency failure (cytolib/BH before package checking) is distinct from this repaired macOS failure.

    Tracing the device failure exposed a second defect: ggsave() can return without producing a figure, or draw on the caller/default device when a Cairo initializer only warns. Publication figures now stage the figure and optional sidecar, require nonempty output, preserve previous files on render/metadata failure and restore them after ordinary publication failures. A failed restore retains and identifies its backup. This is not a multi-file crash-atomic transaction; callers must serialize writers. TIFF and laboratory-report Cairo PDF initializers now stop before drawing if no device was opened.

    Evidence retained under the audit’s hosted-followup/cellreportR directory:

    • Original device/output regression: ten failing assertions. Later TIFF and laboratory PDF initialization regressions each reproduced their failure. Unintended synthetic Rplots output is retained with hashes outside the package; it is excluded from the final exported source.
    • Final graphics, rollback and real PDF reviewer gate: 140 passing assertions, no failures, warnings or skips. The complete final direct suite passes 1,957 assertions, with the reviewer render gate enabled and no skipped tests.
    • Final source archive: R CMD check --as-cran, zero errors, zero warnings, one incoming new-submission/development-version NOTE. Installed tests pass 1,871 assertions with 32 existing CRAN-only skips; these cases are exercised by the complete direct suite above. Examples, donttest examples, vignettes, PDF and HTML manuals pass.
    • Archive SHA-256: 9b0827faee70cd37ba6918c7251ec4047af50214f371c1c434621f3c39938356. All 319 comparable source payloads match; DESCRIPTION changes are standard build reflow and derived author/packaging fields. Git metadata and diagnostic Rplots files are absent. All author metadata and public signatures remain.
    • Actionlint and whitespace checks pass. House lint remains report-only: 250 baseline, 256 final; additions are five synthetic condition fixtures and the explicit backup-recovery warning. No check was disabled or weakened.
    • Independent reviews cover staging, multi-file rollback, retained recovery backups, graphics-device argument compatibility and both initialization guards. No material issue remains from those reviews.

    First use: install R and the README’s platform prerequisites (including XQuartz for Cairo graphics with CRAN R on macOS), then pak::pak("CTTIR/cellreportR"). Construct a ggplot and call cr_save_figure(p, "figure.tiff", dpi = 300, metadata = list(source = "my dataset")). The returned filename is available only after publication succeeds. Actual installed-archive TIFF/PDF exports and their SHA-256 sidecars are checked separately in the local evidence.

    Native hosted macOS qualification follows the authorized main push. No release, submission, manual deployment or source-data modification was performed.

    Original audit

    Baseline: 11e105790487f8964f8fdf6e782b255a46742f09, version 0.2.0.9000. Work takes place in an isolated checkout. The clean original, manuscript-anchor tag/release, source data, author metadata and API-lock snapshots are preserved.

    Purpose and acceptance criteria

    The project converts segmented microscopy measurements into traceable assay analyses, distinguishes cells from independent experimental units, and produces reviewable research/laboratory reports from explicit results. The central acceptance criterion is that the reported analysis level and design support the estimate, uncertainty and sample-size claim actually computed.

    This corrective development version will retain public function signatures, declared dependencies and normal valid grouping keys. Intentional numerical corrections will be documented with a migration path back to the immutable manuscript anchor; existing analyses will not be silently rewritten. Report content, sources and authorship remain caller-owned.

    Findings and roadmap

    Priority Evidence and impact Outcome, changes and validation
    Essential cr_test(level="replicate") computes effect sizes on cells. A seeded fixture gives d=2.12 in the result, versus d=4.29 from the replicate summaries used by the test. The result summary mixes replication levels. Compute effect sizes at the requested level; use replicate effects for both, with the cell result available explicitly. Compare against independently computed unit summaries and validate report/plot consumers. Document changed estimates and intervals.
    Essential .cr_fit_blocked() accepts a treatment completely confounded with plate: a synthetic shift of 20 receives a nominal within-block interval 17.6–22.4. R drops a later block coefficient while retaining the earlier treatment coefficient. Reject non-estimable or saturated blocked designs; retain a skipped-contrast explanation. Test complete confounding, supported crossed designs and row-order invariance.
    Essential cr_power_grid() falls back to observed sizing when the conservative interval spans zero, allowing sufficient=TRUE despite no conservative target. Bounds and vector lengths are also insufficiently checked. Base sufficiency exclusively on the conservative target; validate ordered intervals and compatible lengths. Preserve observed sizing as explicitly descriptive output. Test both signs, crossing-zero and missing intervals against stats::power.t.test().
    Essential cr_batch_key() maps (A | B, C) and (A, B | C) to the same key; missing values also collide with literal <NA>. .cr_stat_groups() uses unescaped text concatenation. Distinct biological batches can be pooled. Refuse ambiguous public keys without changing valid keys; group internal statistics by typed tuples. Verify separate batch control denominators and missing/literal-label cases.
    Essential cr_compare_levels() joins numeric strata using only shared text columns, yielding four rows from two contrasts. .cr_join_design() adds .x/.y suffixes to repeated treatment metadata and breaks valid experiments. Reject ambiguous comparison joins and require explicit keys when needed; share the existing documented cell/design join policy. Exercise imported cells through counting, tests and effect grids.
    Essential The signed-rank branch pairs rows by position and silently truncates unequal arms, while reporting the original counts. No matched-pair identifier is accepted by this interface. Refuse this unidentifiable pairing path with a clear migration to explicitly matched vectors and stats::wilcox.test(..., paired=TRUE). A designed matched-pair API is a separate future enhancement.
    Everyday use README screening code passes a cr_dataset into experiment-only stages and names a nonexistent summarized response column. Replace it with an executed example using the bundled synthetic screen, documented experimental units and actual output columns.
    Reporting integrity The render path writes the optional audit after the report without checking that the paths differ or applying overwrite protection to the audit. Reproduce the collision, protect report/audit destinations before rendering, and retain failure-path evidence. Qualify real PDF/HTML outputs and the existing reviewer browser gate.
    Essential Installed sva confirms the one-row ComBat call errors and returns median centering instead. The output does not identify this substituted method. Refuse unsupported single-channel ComBat; retain explicit median centering and document migration to a scientifically designed feature-by-sample analysis. Test refusal and the actual centering calculation.
    Scientific limitation cr_power_analysis() simulates independent cells before averaging; it has no between-unit random effect or intraclass correlation. Its description overstates hierarchical power modeling. Describe the existing simulation accurately without silently replacing its model. Defer a validated correlated-data power model and new public API.
    Installation Real reviewer downloads and required render tests fail because the template resolves TeX Gyre Heros as an OS font. The minimal toolchain lacks the font package; even after installation the OS font lookup resolves Helvetica. Load the four TeX-distributed font files directly, check them in preflight, and document tex-gyre. Repeat real PDF and browser qualification.
    Release blocker DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21889928 returns HTTP 404 from both doi.org and the Zenodo record API on 2026-10-30. Citation/deposit metadata still labels the current tree 0.2.0 and supplies a historical release date. Remove the unresolved DOI from current public citation metadata, align draft versions and omit unreleased dates; preserve author identities and this prior DOI for investigation. Confirm or mint the correct DOI during authorized deposition.
    Essential integration The bundled Shiny screen has ten compounds sharing dose labels. The effects handler omits by, pooling them into three contrasts; its default control is the first alphabetic dose instead of the declared Vehicle. Target changes can relabel previously computed effects. Add explicit strata with compound selected when available, use the declared control initially, retain strata in plots/downloads, and invalidate stale effects on target or data changes. Verify both in-process and installed-browser journeys.
    Export portability The complete installed test suite passes 1,914 assertions but emits one warning: macOS Quartz ignores the requested TIFF compression. Select native Cairo only when R also reports TIFF support; keep an explicit uncompressed Quartz-configured fallback. This R has Cairo but no native TIFF support, so checking Cairo alone is insufficient. Check actual TIFF compression metadata and rerun the package check.
    Qualification Baseline: 605 tests, 1,810 assertions passed, three render errors from six missing TeX components; no test skips/warnings. Hosted checks at the baseline passed. Install the missing isolated toolchain components, retain the baseline evidence, run API lock, complete tests with the required render gate, clean package checks, first use, documentation and real-browser qualification.

    The API-lock tests remain mandatory and their snapshots are not to be accepted to hide a regression. The version change and migration notes distinguish these corrections from the frozen manuscript software. Publication requires review of affected analyses; no source manuscript or historical result will be modified.

    Authoritative method references: R model aliasing explains why a retained coefficient does not establish independent estimability; R power calculations defines the per-group sample-size calculation used here. The fontspec manual documents loading fonts by filename, including explicit style files. The R bitmap-device documentation describes platform-specific compression support. The sva manual specifies a probe-by-sample matrix and design covariates for ComBat.

    Verification and handover

    Completed repairs include replication-consistent effect estimates, estimable blocked models, unambiguous grouping/joins, conservative sample-size decisions, explicit refusal of unidentified pairing and unsupported single-channel ComBat, report/audit output protection, portable PDF fonts and runnable screening code. The application now keeps selected strata in its effects, forest facets and downloads, initializes the declared control, and invalidates results when the analysis target changes. No API-lock snapshot, manuscript anchor, original checkout or source dataset was changed. Public signatures, authors and declared dependencies are preserved.

    Observed evidence (detailed logs under ../../evidence/cellreportR/):

    • Baseline: 605 tests; 1,810 assertions passed; three real PDF errors from the incomplete TeX environment. The intermediate complete run had 1,850 passing assertions and exposed the font-resolution failures; these were not accepted.
    • After correction: 46 focused tests, 234 assertions, zero failures, errors, warnings or skips. Includes all API locks, analysis/output regressions, the required reviewer render gate, standard PDF and long-content PDF fixtures.
    • Installed-package Chromium gate: all 20 recorded checks pass at 320, 390 and 1,280 px, including keyboard disclosure, escaped text, isolated session URLs, real HTML/PDF/specification/audit downloads, source-change refusal on refresh and captured URLs, and refusal to serve arbitrary source/sibling files. No external browser requests occurred; this is not OS network isolation. The owned loopback server was stopped. The figure-download fixture is only a PDF signature; the report download is a real two-page PDF with embedded TeX Gyre Heros fonts, rendered and visually inspected on both pages.
    • README screening example: 1,340 cells, 73 experimental units and six contrasts; seven Excel sheets checked against their originating table row counts. The exported effect figure was rendered and visually checked after replacing a clipped example subtitle. A real flowCore FCS write/read round trip passed.
    • Existing lint is report-only in CI: 3,456 baseline style findings. Changes introduce no new findings; unrelated formatting is deferred. Actionlint and git diff --check pass. Shellcheck/pyflakes are not installed for actionlint.
    • The complete affected Shiny server/helper suite and API locks pass. The two new application tests contribute 12 passing assertions. Installed-browser use of the ten-compound example yields 30 contrasts against Vehicle; all downloaded estimates and p-values agree with a scripted stratified analysis. Target changes clear stale output. Chart/table dimensions, scrolling, CSV and PNG downloads were exercised; both the table and exported forest plot were visually inspected. Both owned Shiny listeners were stopped.
    • Documentation: 178 built HTML pages, 7,143 local references, no missing files. Pandoc reports deprecated math-option flags from its callers; the build succeeds. No package checks were weakened to hide these diagnostics.
    • Final source archive installs into a fresh library and its first-use analysis returns five finite replicate-level contrasts with correct citation metadata. All 318 matching source files agree byte-for-byte; Git metadata and this audit are absent. No high-confidence private-key and access-token patterns were found in 328 scanned tracked text files under 2 MB (not a history/secrets audit).
    • First complete source-package check: zero errors and check warnings, two notes (new submission/development version; missing optional V8 math renderer). Its installed suite passed 1,914 assertions with zero failures/skips and one TIFF warning. The warning was investigated: this R has Cairo but no native TIFF support. The corrected fallback and actual TIFF metadata pass the focused export/API suite (37 assertions, no warnings). V8 is now installed in the isolated toolchain. The final complete --as-cran check passes with zero errors, zero warnings and one NOTE (new submission/development version). All 1,918 installed-test assertions pass, with zero failures, warnings or skips; both manuals and all vignette rebuilds pass. Native compressed Cairo TIFF output remains a hosted-platform check; the local fallback is verified.

    First use

    Prerequisites: R >= 4.1, the declared imports and optional writexl for the screening workbook. Shiny needs bslib and DT. FCS import uses Bioconductor flowCore. PDF reports need rmarkdown, knitr, Pandoc and XeLaTeX; the TeX Live components installed for this qualification were koma-script, microtype, needspace, lastpage, draftwatermark, tex-gyre and enumitem, alongside the existing base packages. The font files are resolved directly through TeX. Automatic TeX installation was disabled during validation.

    On this machine, dependencies and the isolated installed package are available:

    AUDIT_ROOT=/Users/rh/Documents/GitHub/.repository-audits/cttir-public-20261030
export R_LIBS_USER="$AUDIT_ROOT/evidence/cellreportR/archive-library:$AUDIT_ROOT/tools/R-library"
Rscript --vanilla -e 'library(cellreportR); e <- cr_example_experiment(seed=42, n_cells_per_well=20); r <- cr_test_all(e, "marker_1", "Untreated", level="replicate"); print(attr(r,"summary"))'

    Run the README screening block for the complete QC, unit/cell comparison, power, Excel, figure and numeric-macro workflow. For a separate checkout, install its imports, then use R CMD INSTALL .; do not install the historical GitHub main branch and assume it contains these unpublished corrections.

    Remaining release gates and deferred work

    • Review corrected estimates against each affected manuscript/analysis before adopting this development version. Preserve the immutable historical anchor for exact reproduction. No real study result has been recalculated here.
    • Verify the publication record or obtain the correct DOI during authorized deposition. Prior value 10.5281/zenodo.21889928 returns 404 from both the DOI resolver and Zenodo record API on 2026-10-30. It remains recorded here and in Git history, but is no longer advertised as a current verified citation.
    • Select the final release version/date, update draft deposit metadata, run the hosted OS/R matrix on the accepted commit, and review before publication. No push, release, submission, hosted candidate CI or production deployment has been performed. This qualification used macOS ARM64 and synthetic data.
    • A validated model of between-unit variation for power, an explicit matched- pair API and multi-feature ComBat integration require separately designed scientific work. Existing independent-cell power simulations are scenarios, not a general hierarchical model or guaranteed bound on real study power.
    • Broad style cleanup is outside this corrective release. Deployment access controls, clinical validation and real-user operating procedures remain the responsibility of the intended deployment and are not established by these local fixtures.
